prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 3 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone; image 3 is the approved last panel of the previous part of this scene's board. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown; image 3: panel 1 of this sheet, repeated exactly: the same camera, place, light and mannequins.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin; Father is the yellow mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One painted storyboard image arranged four panels across and three down, with eleven vertical panels in shot order and the bottom-right cell left blank. Use plain gutters, with no lettering, labels, symbols or arrows. Kasun is a medium-height, lean red artist's mannequin; Anudi is an average-height, slender blue artist's mannequin, both smooth and unmarked. Render the setting and props realistically. Soft overcast early-morning daylight, wet patched asphalt, damp concrete pavement and open kerb drainage remain consistent throughout; no rain is falling. Keep a restrained grey-green grade, gentle warm highlights and subdued amber light from the food three-wheeler. Anudi's handset has an orange back, a transparent protective case and a black front. Her navy folding umbrella stays open, its shaft held in her left hand; her structured tan handbag, with brass-coloured fittings, hangs by its strap from her right shoulder. Maintain the same mannequin proportions, props and light across all panels.

Geography: The narrow pavement runs horizontally through the scene, with the road and open drain along its camera-facing edge. Kasun's compact food three-wheeler occupies the vending bay at screen left, beneath a faded blue shop awning with warm light underneath; this awning is the recurring landmark. Behind the bay are weathered shop shutters, while a pale green building section and stained concrete boundary wall extend toward screen right along Anudi's departure path. Kasun stands left of their conversation gap, with the three-wheeler behind and farther left; Anudi stands on the right. Every camera remains on the roadward side of their line, looking toward the pavement and frontages. The departure continues laterally toward screen right along this same pavement, never away into depth.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Roadward side at the shared master position; standing head height, 40mm feel, locked waist-up two-shot. Background: The three-wheeler and faded blue awning return clearly on frame left behind red. Pale green frontage and the stained wall remain on frame right behind blue, with the open umbrella above blue. Red stands screen left with its chest facing right and its head turned three-quarter right toward blue, both empty hands resting low near its waist. Blue stands screen right with its chest facing left and its head held three-quarter left, its near-side right hand still holding the phone against the right side of its head. Blue's far-side left hand grips the umbrella shaft at waist height, and the tan bag rests against its near right hip.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Roadward side on the established axis; standing head height, 35mm feel, balanced mid-torso two-shot. Background: The faded blue shop awning and softly lit three-wheeler stay on frame left. The green frontage and concrete wall stay on frame right, with the umbrella canopy above blue. Red stands left with its chest facing right and its head turned three-quarter right toward blue, its empty hands below the crop near its waist. Blue stands right with its chest facing left and its head turned three-quarter left toward red. Blue's right arm is lowered, keeping the phone below the crop on its near side, while its far-side left hand holds the umbrella shaft and the tan bag strap stays over its near shoulder.
PANEL 3 (row 2, column 1) — Roadward side, farther back and slightly elevated; approximately two metres high looking gently downward, 24mm feel, full-figure vertical wide shot. Background: The complete three-wheeler and faded blue shop awning anchor frame left, with the warm serving bay beneath. The same pale green frontage and stained boundary wall extend across frame right beside the open departure path; wet pavement, the drain and patched road fill the foreground, with utility poles and cables above. Red stands on the left third beside the three-wheeler opening, chest and head angled screen right toward blue, with both empty hands lowered. Blue stands centre-right, half-turned into a side-on rightward departure pose, chest and head facing screen right and feet set for a lateral step across the frame. Blue's left hand is now on the near, camera-facing side holding the open umbrella shaft, while its right hand holds the phone low on the far side and the tan bag is partly obscured against its far right hip. Clear pavement remains ahead of blue toward the right edge.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
